name: Mam, Central
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: [Godfrey & Collins 1987:93] Lingüísticamente el mam que se habla en Comitancillo tiene características tanto del área norte como del área sur. Utiliza vocablos clave del sur como: /ičin/ hombre, /qya/ mujer y /neʔṣ̌/ bebé, pero también presenta rasgos del norte: como lo son algunas semejanzas lexicales y la penúltima sílaba tónica. [López & Collins 1991:23] Por ejemplo, en el diccionario, la palabra máq'tzil en mam central es seguida por (meq'tzál, máq'tzal). Este significa que en el área norteña se pronuncia la palabra con la sílaba tónica final, mientras que en el área sureña, la sílaba tónica es penúltima.
new_statements.translation: [1987:93] Linguistically, the Mam spoken in Comitancillo has characteristics of both the northern and the southern area. It uses southern key words such as /ičin/ 'man', /qya/ 'woman' and /neʔš/ 'baby', but it also shows northern traits, such as certain lexical similarities and the penultimate stressed (tonic) syllable. [1991:23] For example, in the dictionary the central-Mam word máq'tzil is followed by (meq'tzál, máq'tzal). This means that in the northern area the word is pronounced with the tonic syllable final, whereas in the southern area the tonic syllable is penultimate.

QUOTE. Godfrey & Collins 1987, printed p.93 (running head 'TUIMUJ 93'), entry 'Comitancillo, SM (35)', third paragraph, reads on the page image exactly: 'Linguisticamente el mam que se habla en Comitancillo tiene caracteristicas tanto del area no…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Comitancillo (central San Marcos) Mam the stressed syllable is the penultimate one; the SIL authors treat this as one of the traits Comitancillo shares with (their) northern area, in contrast to e.g. San Martín Sacatepéquez in the south, which tends toward a final stressed syllable. The companion Comitancillo verb dictionary marks the tonic syllable on every headword: central máq'tzil (penult) vs northern (Ixtahuacán) meq'tzál (final) vs southern (Chiquirichapa) máq'tzal (penult).
new_statements.exceptions: The survey states no exceptions. However, the stress-marked headwords of López & Collins 1991 (same authorship, Comitancillo variety) are mostly penultimate (áb'tzil, ájb'il, mejéb'il, méltz'il, b'ántsil, kyímsil, oqxénil, úk'tzil, xmákil..) but show a recurrent final-stressed class, typically CVC-root infinitives whose penult carries a reduced vowel or none (meqól, mikól/mekól, miqúl, milól, kchol, saqchál) and some longer forms (meltz'ajíl, tilk'ajíl); a footnote also says certain person forms are distinguished by 'un cambio en la sílaba tónica'. So the one-line 'penultimate' characterisation is a simplification and the system may be partly weight/vowel-quality sensitive, as in Northern Mam; no source seen states the actual rule for Comitancillo.
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic word-level remark in a dialect-survey community profile (SIL fieldworkers; Collins resident in Comitancillo from ~1980); the dictionary marks the tonic syllable on citation-form (infinitive) headwords 'sólo para fines de comparación'. England 1990:221 places the rest of San Marcos (hence Comitancillo) in her 'Mam del sur' region, for which she reports penultimate stress (Ostuncalco data, enclitics not counted), consistent with the SIL remark; Godfrey & Collins's own 'mam central' group (p.110) = Comitancillo, San Miguel Ixtahuacán, Concepción Tutuapa, Tejutla, San Lorenzo, Río Blanco.
new_statements.identity_note: mamc1234 is a Glottolog 'Bookkeeping' languoid for the retired ISO 639-3 code mvc 'Mam, Central' (Ethnologue 15: San Marcos Dept., 10 towns; alt. names Comitancillo Mam, Mam Marquense, 'Western Mam/Mam Occidental'), merged in 2009 (CR 2008-055, N. England) into mam = Mam, Glottolog mamm1241 (Mayan, Mamean). The quoted statement is specifically about the Comitancillo (San Marcos) variety, the reference dialect of SIL's 'mam central' (Godfrey & Collins 1987:110: Comitancillo, San Miguel Ixtahuacán, Concepción Tutuapa, Tejutla, San Lorenzo, Río Blanco; López & Collins 1991:21 add Tajumulco and Ixchiguán). In England's (1990, 2017) regional scheme there is no 'central' group: Comitancillo falls under 'Mam del sur' (rest of San Marcos + Quetzaltenango; penultimate stress per Ostuncalco data), while Ethnologue itself notes that San Miguel Ixtahuacán and Concepción Tutuapa lean toward Northern Mam (weight-sensitive stress, England 1983). Any catalog entry should therefore be filed under Mam (mamm1241) as the Comitancillo / central San Marcos dialect, alongside the existing Northern (Ixtahuacán, Todos Santos), Southern (Ostuncalco) and Western (Tacaná) statements.
